Build the app described below in an existing Next.js 16 project (App Router, React 19, strict TypeScript).

Stack: Material UI (`@mui/material` 9) is set up with its Next.js App Router integration, light and dark color schemes and `CssBaseline`; `@mui/icons-material`, `@mui/x-charts` and `@mui/x-data-grid` are installed, and the Material UI documentation is in the `docs/` folder, which you can read (start with `docs/README.md`).

Task: Lumen needs a command palette. Inside a shared app layout with three screens (a dashboard at `/`, projects at `/projects`, members at `/members`), pressing Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac) opens a palette with a search field. Results are grouped under "Pages" (the three screens), "Actions" ("Create project", "Invite member", "Toggle theme") and "Recent" (three recently opened projects). Typing filters every group; arrow keys move the highlight and Enter runs it. "Invite member" opens a dialog with an email field. A visible button in the header (with the shortcut shown next to it) opens the palette too, so it works on phones.

# Material UI documentation (local copy)

This folder is a local copy of the official Material UI and MUI X documentation for agents
(`llms.txt`), snapshotted on the date in the benchmark's context manifest. Everything listed
here is already set up in the project.

- `llms.txt`: the official Material UI documentation index. Every link points at a local page
  under `material-ui/`.
- `x-llms.txt`: the official MUI X index (charts, data grid, date pickers, tree view). Pages are
  under `x/`. Installed: `@mui/x-charts` and `@mui/x-data-grid` (the free, MIT-licensed
  packages). Date pickers, tree view and every Pro or Premium feature are **not** installed.
- Also installed: `@mui/material`, `@mui/icons-material`, Emotion, and `@mui/material-nextjs`.
  The root layout already mounts `AppRouterCacheProvider`, `ThemeProvider` (theme in
  `app/theme.ts`, CSS variables with light and dark color schemes), `CssBaseline` and
  `InitColorSchemeScript`, as in `material-ui/integrations/nextjs.md`.

content.text:
Let me think about what could hang `/projects` specifically. Dashboard (`/`) renders fine, but `/projects` and `/members` are in a route group with a server layout that imports a client `AppShell`. The page navigation never completing suggests a render loop or hang during SSR/hydration on those routes.

Candidates:
-   `useColorScheme` + `setIsMac` in an effect are fine on `/` too, so those aren't route-specific.
-   `metadata` exports in server pages are fine.
-   A route group `(app)` layout alongside a root `app/page.tsx`: each page has its own `AppShell`, so navigating between them remounts the shell, and the palette state resets on navigation. That is a UX problem, but not a hang.

The most likely culprit is the `page.goto` waiting for the `load` event while something keeps the page busy: the `Snackbar` with `open={notice !== null}` and an `Alert` child with `{notice}` is fine, but the Next.js dev server is also prefetching `<Link>` targets, which for dynamic shells can stall.

I can't reproduce it without running the app, so I'll remove every risky pattern rather than guess. I'll make one real shared layout instead of two parallel shells. I'll move all three pages into one route group so that a single `AppShell` persists, and `app/page.tsx` will re-export the dashboard page from the group. I'll also drop the `Link` prefetching in the header, use plain links for navigation, and make the shell's client-only pieces mount after hydration.
